scope: Theorem 1.2 (Local C2 strong cosmic censorship) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed M > 0 and 0 < a < M, there exists ϵ > 0 such that the data in Uϵ = {d ∈ D : p10(d − (h∗, K∗)) < ϵ} whose full maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum developments admit a C2 future extension form a meagre subset of Uϵ. Equivalently, the future-inextendible data contain a countable intersection of relatively open dense subsets of Uϵ.
